title: feat(launcher): --bot-mobile-keyboard toggle + crash-safe self-updater
body:
## Summary

Two changes.

### `--bot-mobile-keyboard`
BB 150 (2026-07-11) added `--bot-mobile-keyboard`: an opt-in mobile keyboard visual-viewport behavior where editable-field focus shrinks `visualViewport.height` while the layout viewport stays fixed. Default off, mobile profiles only. Exposed as a Behavior slide-toggle next to Force Touch; emits the bare flag only when enabled.

### Crash-safe self-updater
The auto-updater rebuilt in place with `neu build` while the app was running. On Windows the running exe and `resources.neu` are locked, so the rebuild wrote partial/corrupt artifacts — on next launch Neutralino couldn't load the app and fell back to its default welcome page, leaving reinstall as the only recovery.

Now:
- The update builds into a separate **staging** repo (`<install>/BotBrowser-update`), so nothing live is touched during download/build, and the staged bundle is verified (exe + `resources.neu` present) before being offered.
- Applying the update writes a **detached swap script** that waits for the current process to exit (by PID), then atomically renames the staged `dist/BotBrowserLauncher` over the live one, records the new commit, and relaunches — **rolling back** to the old bundle if the swap fails.
- A build failure now leaves the current install **completely untouched** instead of corrupting it.

Swap logic (Windows `.bat` and Unix `.sh` branches) verified in a sandbox, including the locked-binary case: while the exe is held open a move is denied (reproducing the old corruption), and the script correctly waits for release before swapping.

**Note:** existing corrupted installs need one manual reinstall to get onto the new updater; from then on updates are safe. The Neutralino-runtime bits (detached process surviving `app.exit()`, `NL_PID` availability) can only be confirmed with a packaged-app smoke test.

title: feat(launcher): Memory & Storage controls, new flags, running-profile edit, proxy Check IP cancel, editor search
body:
## Summary

### New flags
- **`--bot-video-fps`** (ENT Tier2): actual[:reported] video cadence input next to FPS.
- **`--proxy-pac-url`**: PAC source entry (trusted PAC request-callback workflow).
- **`--disable-quic`**: toggle to keep SOCKS5 UDP fallback off QUIC/HTTP3.
- **`--bot-js-heap-size-limit` / `--bot-storage-quota`**: new Advanced "Memory & Storage" section — Default / profile / real / Custom(bytes), mirroring the FPS-mode pattern. Empty = no flag (kernel default). Byte values validated as positive integers both at save and at launch, so malformed hand-edited/imported profile JSON can't emit an invalid flag or inject extra CLI args.

### Proxy Check IP
- The check can now be cancelled: the button becomes a red **Stop** while running. `ShellService.run` accepts an `AbortSignal` and kills the spawned `curl` via `updateSpawnedProcess(pid,'exit')` (handles the abort-before-pid race); `curl` also gained `--max-time 30` so a stalled transfer can't hang forever.
- A shown/in-flight result can no longer be mis-attributed to a different proxy — clearing or editing the proxy tears down / invalidates the check (identity compared by signature; success branch guards on abort + identity).

### Editor UX
- **Running profiles are now editable** (previously blocked). The editor shows a banner and a save-time snackbar noting changes take effect on next launch. Safe: the browser-exit handler only updates in-memory status and never rewrites the profile, and a running instance uses the bot profile written at launch.
- **Section nav gains a filter** that narrows the section list (per-section keyword index) and **highlights matching content** — section titles, sub-titles, field labels, and toggles light up and the first hit scrolls into view, so field-level terms like `heap`, `quic`, `pac`, `timezone` jump straight to the control.

### Layout
- Quick-proxy dialog widened to 620px (maxWidth 95vw), content min-width removed, so the four action buttons fit one row without forcing horizontal page overflow on small windows.
- Check IP spinner+label wrapped in an inline-flex span (MDC label intact); button-row wraps gracefully when cramped.

title: fix(launcher): CLI-flag honesty, tri-state Mobile, legacy migration, Node 24.15 pin
body:
- **CLI-flag honesty**: default-on toggles (debugger / always-active / console-message + 4 noise flags) now only emit `=false` when the user explicitly overrides — values matching BB's own defaults no longer appear on the command line or in the CLI preview. Free-text locale fields treat literal `auto` as no-emit. Local DNS drops the redundant `off` option (kernel default = off) for `Default (off)`. V8Log hides the duplicate `none` mode and gates the directory input on a chosen mode. `--bot-title` moves into `buildProfileFlags` so the preview matches the real spawn. `botConfigNoiseTextRects` form default now matches BB's default-on (was missing the fallback).
- **Mobile tri-state**: `Mobile Mode` becomes a `Default / On / Off` mat-select. The previous binary slide-toggle couldn't distinguish "inherit profile" from "force desktop" and silently broke Android profiles when a user flipped it off.
- **Legacy profile migration**: profiles persisted from the earlier UI carry boolean `false` for Mobile / LocalDns that meant "no override" under the old emit rules; new code would re-interpret those as explicit Off and silently force desktop or re-emit redundant `--bot-local-dns=false`. Form initializers now coerce legacy `false → null` on load, the service drops the `v === false` LocalDns branch on both the proxy and legacy paths, and `botV8Log='none'` (no longer a visible mode) normalizes to the Off sentinel so the mat-select renders correctly. Mobile mat-select pre-selects `Default (from profile)` on undefined.
- **Hardening**: `emitToggle` switched to a nullish check so an explicit `null` from hand-edited or imported profile JSON no longer produces `--bot-config-noise-*=null`.
- **Node 24.15 pin**: Angular 22's engine constraint (`^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26`) rejects 24.13.0 (a Russian-speaking user hit `EBADENGINE` on every Angular package). Bumped `.nvmrc`, all three setup scripts, and added an `engines` field to `package.json` so `npm ci` warns up front. Install scripts now version-check the existing private Node dir and re-extract on mismatch so re-running setup actually upgrades a stale install instead of short-circuiting. README clarifies the Node LTS stance.

We’ve begun running BotBrowser in production and appreciate the frequent updates. However, our Docker/CI builds currently hard-code GitHub release asset URLs. When asset filenames/paths advance, builds start failing with 404 Not Found until we manually change the Dockerfile. A small installer CLI (e.g., botbrowser install) that resolves the latest compatible build would eliminate this fragility.

Current behavior
Example of what breaks today (asset name/date changes → 404 in CI):

```
# Fails when the exact asset URL changes
```

Stealth issue
body:
I've just carried out a few tests with my [chromate](https://github.com/Eth3rnit3/chromate) project and unless I'm using something incorrectly, but I've made sure to provide only the arguments that are present in the demo. I lose efficiency against an unpatched version of chrome running in a docker container with xfvb. 

```log
[Chromate] 2024-11-20 21:08:45 DEBUG: Starting browser with args: ["/Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium", "--user-data-dir=/Users/eth3rnit3/.config/google-chrome/Default", "--bot-profile=$HOME/Downloads/chrome130-macarm.enc", "--disable-audio-output", "--no-sandbox", "--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled", "--headless=new", "--remote-debugging-port=50177"]
```

The only gain is on pixelscan where the ip is not interfered with, but this seems to add a problem at the webGL vendor level, cloudflare detects abnormal activity and the use of the mouse via CDP is detected.

You can see the differences with docker + xfvb here https://github.com/Eth3rnit3/chromate/pull/15/files
